event.description: Join Whitney Educators in the Museum's lobby to create a drawing inspired by Biennial artist Kelly Akashi's Monument (Altadena). Draw the people, places, objects, and ideas that matter most to you. Monument (Altadena) stands as a symbol of the widespread losses suffered in Altadena, California, during the wildfires of January 2025. After Kelly Akashi’s home and studio burned down, the chimney was the only structure left standing. The artist worked with a mason to rebuild it piece by piece, alongside a reconstruction of her home’s walkway, in luminous glass brick.  Explaining her decision to create this work Akashi said, “I've just gotten very interested in the idea that if this recreation of my chimney is a kind of monument for what's happened, that it shouldn't be made of a singular mass material, that it should be reconstructed with the same labor that the original chimney was constructed in with brick laying. Because I really love this idea that not only is that labor going back into the reconstruction of the chimney, but that it's also a monument made of many parts, many bricks, and many pieces.”
event.name: All Ages Artmaking: Drawing what matters most

event.description: Join Whitney Educators to explore the art of printmaking inspired by the exhibition Mabel Dwight: Cool Head, Warm Heart. Mabel Dwight found inspiration by observing the people and places of New York City. Create your own print inspired by your unique perspective on the city. Think about a place, person, object, or everyday moment that represents New York to you, then transform your idea into a print. Dwight believed that making art required “a cool head and a warm heart” so it could become a “living influence on the world.” She found her voice in lithography, a printmaking method known for its swooping lines and seamless gradients. This democratic medium became her main way of portraying her constant subject: the people and places of New York. Dwight’s vision centered on dignity across social and economic divides. Her crowd scenes show individuals drawn with gently curving lines, dramatic lighting, and delicate highlights. Her portraits feature expressive faces, while her more political images can feel theatrical. Whether showing people selling balloons, strolling home, or waiting for the day to pass, her subjects share an inner glow she called “the stuff of life.” Dwight gathered these moments by roaming the city, sketching what she saw, then turning them into prints that could be widely shared.
event.name: All Ages Printmaking: Inspired by Mabel Dwight

event.description: The Whitney Free Second Sundays Storytime series continues strong, teaming up with independent bookstores to showcase diverse voices and fresh perspectives that will captivate our youngest visitors. We're excited to launch a fantastic four-month partnership with Librería Comunitaria Barco de Papel and Centro Cultural, a vibrant community-run bookstore and cultural center. Their mission is to bring the magic of the Spanish language and bilingual literature to the heart of Flushing and Elmhurst, Queens—and now, right here at the Whitney! Join us for Storytime with the incredible Paula Ortiz, co-founder of Barco de Papel, along with our passionate volunteer readers. They'll be bringing to life stunning art-inspired books that celebrate the beauty of storytelling in both Spanish and English. Don’t miss out on this unforgettable experience—be a part of a celebration that honors the future of storytelling with us! En español La serie Hora del Cuento, parte del Segundo domingo gratuito del Whitney, sigue creciendo, en colaboración con librerías independientes para destacar voces diversas y nuevas perspectivas que cautivarán a nuestros visitantes más jóvenes. Nos entusiasma dar inicio a una fantástica colaboración de cuatro meses con Barco de Papel, una vibrante librería y centro cultural gestionada por la comunidad. Su misión es llevar la magia del idioma español y la literatura bilingüe al corazón de Flushing y Elmhurst, Queens, ¡y ahora también aquí, en el Whitney! Acompáñanos en la Hora del Cuento con la increíble Paula Ortiz, cofundadora de Barco de Papel, junto con nuestros apasionados lectores voluntarios. Darán vida a maravillosos libros inspirados en arte, que celebran la belleza de la narración tanto en español como en inglés. No te pierdas esta inolvidable experiencia: ¡sé parte de una celebración que honra el futuro de la narración de cuentos!
event.name: Storytime
